title: Operational contract: latency bands, availability budgets, and deployment thresholds
creator: Sofia Nguyen
description: Purpose: Produce an operational contract (PRD-level) that codifies latency bands, availability budgets, error-budgeting rules, and automated deployment thresholds for the Hosted API and Dedicated offering. This ticket captures requirements, acceptance criteria, and rollout gating rules so engineering and SRE can implement alerts, automated rollbacks, and Console UI surfaces. Scope: Hosted API (text-generation, chat, embeddings) + Dedicated core API surface. Out of scope for this ticket: private on-prem packaging and per-customer legal SLA text (handled by enterprise contracting).
acceptance_criteria: Define per-endpoint latency bands (P50, P95) and text-length buckets; documented in the PRD and published to the Console knowledge page.
Specify availability targets and monthly error budgets for Hosted API (standard/free/enterprise tiers) and Dedicated clusters; values agreed by PM, SRE, and Sales.
Create rollout gating rules: canary traffic %s, minimum observation window, and quantified thresholds for latency and error regressions that trigger automated rollback or progressive rollout pause.
Provide concrete automation rules (Datadog/Console watch) that map metrics to actions: alert, pause rollout, rollback. Alerts must include runbook links and owner on-call rotations.
Implement synthetic checks and benchmark harness for each endpoint; results must be reproducible and stored in the performance dashboard with baseline history for 90 days.
All thresholds and rules must be encoded as configuration files in the infra repo (PR + review) so deployments are reproducible, not hard-coded in service binaries.
A smoke test checklist and post-deploy validation steps are created and validated by QA before release cutover.
Stakeholder sign-off from SRE lead, Runtime engineering lead, and Head of Product recorded in the ticket comments.
decision_notes: Use 'latency bands' approach instead of single SLO per endpoint to reflect different prompt lengths and model classes (short/medium/long contexts).
Hosted API default latency targets are intentionally looser than Dedicated to reflect multi-tenant resource variability; Dedicated will have stronger availability targets tied to committed capacity.

Error budgets are monetary/operationally meaningful: for Hosted API standard tier we propose 99.7% availability per month (error budget = 0.3%); for Enterprise/Dedicated 99.95% per month. These are proposals pending SRE risk review.

Rollout canary policy: start at 1% traffic for 2 hours, then 10% for 12 hours, then 30% for 24 hours, full rollout thereafter — each step requires no >2x baseline error rate and no >15% increase in P95 latency over baseline.

Automated rollback triggers: sustained error rate >1% for 15 minutes or 4x baseline for 5 minutes; P95 latency increase >50% sustained for 10 minutes. These thresholds balance false positives vs risk to customers.
We will expose these operational contracts in Console as readable 'Service Contracts' so customers can understand expected behavior for Hosted vs Dedicated offerings.
